What happened narrative: During pig trap receiver door opening procedure, residual pressure of 45 psig remained trapped behind the barrel isolation gate valve. Crude spray struck the maintenance technician helmet and protective suit. Technician had not verified pressure bleed gauge prior to loosening rapid-opening closure clamps.

A flange connection on the suction header of booster pump unit 2 developed a sudden spray leak at the Darfield pump station. Sump containment and oily water separator captured the released light crude oil. Control room shut down main line and dispatched emergency response crew.

Trenching machine operated by contractor struck a 10-inch lateral pipeline during tie-in activities on the Peace River section. The lateral had been marked with survey stakes but one-call ticket depth verification potholing was not completed prior to mechanical excavation.

Sour natural gas release occurred from a 1/2-inch instrument tubing fitting downstream of separator vessel V-12. Ambient H2S detection monitors alarmed at 10 ppm, triggering automatic facility ESD and deluge. Station personnel evacuated safely to designated muster points. Zero injuries.

Slope inclinometer detected accelerated thaw settlement ground movement on right-of-way kilometer post 142. Preventative line depressurization conducted after high bending strains observed. Minor seepage identified at girth weld during investigative bell hole excavation.

Contractor crew performed hot work welding on support stanchion adjacent to glycol dehydrator without conducting atmospheric combustible gas testing. Flash fire occurred when fugitive vapors ignited. One contract welder sustained severe facial burns requiring airlift hospitalization.

NGL vapor leak detected at meter manifold packing gland during product batch changeover from propane to butane. Automatic gas detection initiated ESD, isolating valve manifold within 45 seconds. Perimeter flare ignited released vapor safely without damage to equipment.
